data.narrative:
Collaborative Robotics, founded by Brad Porter, is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $150M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private comparables—Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), Hadrian ($1.6B, Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B, Series C)—alongside one public comparable in the robotics sector.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier to the last post-money valuation of $500M, yielding $950M. The peer-median approach anchors to the median valuation of the four comparables at $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $1.8B. The peer set reflects typical frontier-tech robotics funding, capturing both Series B and early Series C benchmarks.

Synthesizing these methods produces a valuation range of $808M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $1.3B. The gap between stage-progression ($950M) and peer-median ($1.6B) reflects uncertainty around whether Collaborative Robotics' operating metrics and market position track closer to earlier-stage or more mature peers within the robotics cohort. Key variables affecting placement within this range include revenue traction, gross margin profile, and customer concentration relative to the comparable set.
